themes.name: Critical Thinking Enhancement
themes.definition: The use of AI tools to develop or improve students' critical thinking skills, including analysis, inference, evaluation, and problem-solving, across various educational contexts.
evidence: [Sánchez-Guerrero2024] ChatGPT, being a language model based on artificial intelligence schemes, contributes to critical thinking in first semester undergraduate students.
[Dmitrenko2025] The article highlights the influence of artificial intelligence (AI), in particular ChatGPT, on the development of critical thinking during ESP classes.
[Cai2025] It is found that the intervention of the AR-based embodied conversational agent significantly enhanced students’ critical thinking, inquisitiveness and learning motivation.

themes.name: Creativity Development with Generative AI
themes.definition: Employing generative AI technologies to enhance students' creative thinking and output in activities such as writing, design, and artistic creation.
evidence: [Chiu2025] generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), such as ChatGPT, has been adopted to facilitate students’ diverse thinking to promote their creativity.
[Wei2025] AIGC significantly enhances the creativity of students from various disciplines.

[Gil-Ruíz2025] The use of AI applications focused on image and video generation provided participants with an artistic mediator, which allowed them, under specific instructions, to configure photographs and videos tailored to the communicative objectives of their narratives.

themes.name: AI in Language Education
themes.definition: Application of AI tools to support language learning and teaching, particularly in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and other language contexts, focusing on skills like writing, debate, and communication.
evidence: [Butarbutar2025] Debate competence is essential in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning... This study aims to evaluate the impact of AI Debater technology on the debate performance of EFL learners.
[Elmouhtadi2025] GenAI contributes to the learning of French as a foreign language (FFL) in a hybrid learning context.
[Lin2025d] This study addresses the gap in research on how Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools support L2 learners in critical reading and writing.

themes.name: Ethical and Reflective AI Use
themes.definition: Focusing on the ethical implications of AI in education and using AI tools to promote reflective practice and ethical awareness among students.
evidence: [Zhang2025d] The “Virtual Reflection” platform combines interactive AI-powered modules with offline discussions to teach Deepfake-related ethics, fostering critical thinking and ethical awareness.
[Grande2024] Generative AI and LLMs also raised ethical questions and concerns for computing educators and professionals.
[Huang2026b] This study investigates the application of ChatGPT as a tool to support reflective learning among nursing students.

themes.name: Integration of AI with Immersive Technologies
themes.definition: Combining AI with augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), or other immersive technologies to create enhanced learning environments.
evidence: [Cai2025] Generative AI plus AR: a novel embodied conversational agent in an interactive learning environment.
[Bernetti2024] Integrating Virtual Reality and Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Planning.
[Suyidno2025] Augmented reality, artificial intelligence, and local wisdom-based renewable energy learning media.

themes.name: Methodological Diversity in AI Education Research
themes.definition: Employment of various research methods, including mixed-methods, quantitative, qualitative, and experimental designs, to study the impact of AI in education.
evidence: [Rovira-Collado2025] The research employs a mixed-methods approach.
[Khotimah2024] This quantitative study focused on an experimental group using a onegroup pretest-posttest research design.
[Chiu2025] This quasi-experimental study involved 45 students from a university in central Taiwan.

themes.name: Student Autonomy and Self-Regulated Learning
themes.definition: Using AI tools to foster student autonomy, self-regulation, and reflective learning practices in educational settings.
evidence: [Elmouhtadi2025] GenAI, which is widely integrated into students' practices, supports the co-construction of linguistic competencies, and fosters the development of autonomy, critical thinking, and ethical awareness.

[Huang2026b] A structured AI-assisted reflective activity was designed to guide nursing students through six reflective stages: goal setting, planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and adjustment.
[Pdurean2025] Students were highly selective about the code they chose to test, suggesting that on-request execution of generated code promoted critical thinking.

themes.name: AI Applications in STEM and Technical Disciplines
themes.definition: Implementation of AI in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and technical courses to enhance skills like problem-solving, logical thinking, and scientific thinking.
evidence: [Bouamor2025] Evaluating GenAI's Effectiveness for Students with Varied Programming Backgrounds in a Software Development Course.
[Bokan2025] Enhancing Logical Thinking Skills of Future Informatics Teachers through Artificial Intelligence.

[Hussein2025] The study aimed to identify the impact of artificial intelligence technologies and active learning on enhancing the capabilities of material engineering students in problem-solving and scientific thinking.

data.meta_observations: The analysis reveals a strong emphasis on critical thinking enhancement across most abstracts, often paired with creativity development. Research methods are diverse, with frequent use of mixed-methods and experimental designs. AI tools, particularly ChatGPT and generative AI, are prevalently integrated into various educational contexts, from language learning to STEM disciplines. Ethical considerations and reflective practices are emerging themes, though less frequent.
data.grounding_notes: All themes and evidence are derived solely from explicitly stated text in the abstracts, adhering to anti-hallucination rules. Some abstracts have quality notes indicating missing elements (e.g., no quantitative data), but this does not affect the inductive analysis based on available text. Confidence is high for all themes due to direct mentions in multiple abstracts.
